name.text: Functions in Real Life — maximizing the area of a fenced plot

questiontext.text:
A farmer has {@perimeter@} metres of fencing to enclose a rectangular plot against an existing straight wall (so only three sides need fencing: two equal widths \(w\) and one length \(l\), opposite the wall).

The area enclosed, as a function of the width \(w\), is

\[ A(w) = w({@perimeter@}-2w). \]

Find the maximum possible area, in square metres.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
\(A(w)=w({@perimeter@}-2w)={@Aexpand@}\) is a downward-opening parabola in \(w\) (the coefficient of \(w^2\) is negative), so it has a maximum at its vertex.

The vertex occurs at \(w={@wvertex@}\), but that is the width that gives the maximum — you still need to substitute it back into \(A(w)\) to get the maximum area:

\[ A({@wvertex@}) = {@wvertex@}({@perimeter@}-2({@wvertex@})) = {@ta@}\ \text{m}^2. \]

node.description: Correct maximum area (not just the optimal width)?
